name: Eiffel Tower
desc: Yes, it's a cliché. It's also 330 meters of sparkle every hour after dark — and the lawn view is free until you can afford the summit.

name: Louvre Museum
desc: A palace stuffed with 35,000 artworks. The Mona Lisa is tiny; the ego boost of finally going is enormous. Wear comfy shoes.

name: Sacré-Cœur Basilica
desc: Climb Montmartre's steps, wander in for free, and watch all of Paris pretend to be a postcard below your feet.

name: Musée d'Orsay
desc: Van Gogh and Monet living inside a gorgeous old train station. That giant clock window is the photo you've been saving up for.

name: Jardin du Luxembourg
desc: Free chairs by the fountain, toy sailboats, chess grandpas. Grab a baguette and live your best six-euro afternoon.

name: Canal Saint-Martin
desc: Iron footbridges, cheap wine on the quay, locals doing absolutely nothing beautifully. Your future picnic headquarters.

name: Père Lachaise Cemetery
desc: The world's most famous cemetery: Wilde, Piaf, Morrison. Gothic, leafy, free, and weirdly peaceful at golden hour.

name: Marché des Enfants Rouges
desc: Paris's oldest market, tucked in the Marais since 1615. Eat your way from Morocco to Japan for the price of one museum ticket.

name: Arc de Triomphe
desc: Climb 284 steps for the view the Eiffel can't give you: the Eiffel itself, plus twelve avenues spinning like a compass.

name: Sainte-Chapelle
desc: A 13th-century jewel box where the walls are basically all stained glass. Go on a sunny day and let it wreck you.
